      "answer": "The general duty to attempt rescues of strangers when one can help is an IMPERFECT (wide) positive duty in Kantian ethics. Re-typing the governing duty as IMPERFECT keeps A0 preferable, since giving the dose to Ben realises the same end—saving life—far more effectively than A1. Therefore, after confirming liberty is unaffected, Rawlsian priority passes to the primary-goods stage. Survival is a core primary good and part of basic-interest security. The least-advantaged person faces certain death under either action, so the difference principle treats the two actions as equal for her. Maximin then permits the option that benefits others without worsening the worst-off: giving the dose to Ben.",
